text:
Everyone says prompt engineering is dead. Wrong.

I cut our support-bot error rate from 14% to 5% last month by rewriting one system prompt: added 3 worked examples, banned the word 'certainly', and told it to ask one clarifying question before answering.

Save this if you ship LLM features.
AI will replace every software engineer by December. I've said it before and I'll say it again.

I spent 40 hours a month on invoice reconciliation. Now it takes 3.

Here's the setup: export the CSV from your bank, paste 50 rows at a time into Claude with a prompt listing your vendor names, and ask for a table of mismatches. Then I review only the flagged ones.

Not magic, still saves a full work week.

OpenAI just dropped another model. Cool. Anyway.

Here's how to actually decide whether to switch: take your 20 worst real prompts, run both models, and compare outputs blind. Takes 30 minutes and beats every benchmark chart.
ChatGPT is 100% accurate if you prompt it right. Hallucinations are just a skill issue.

3 things I learned building my first RAG app:

1. Chunk size matters more than the embedding model
2. Add metadata filters before you add a reranker
3. Evaluate on 30 real questions, not vibes

Follow me for more notes from the trenches.
Big news in AI today!! The future is here!! Things are changing FAST. Are you ready?? 🚀🚀

My grandma asked me what AI is. I told her it's autocomplete that read the whole internet. She said, 'so like your uncle.'

I have not stopped laughing.

Reply 'PROMPT' and I'll DM you my 47-page AI cheat sheet.

It's the same framework I used to grow three accounts. Most people overcomplicate AI. Simple works.

A model scored 90% on a coding benchmark, so software jobs are over?

The benchmark is 164 short Python functions. Real work is ambiguous tickets, legacy code and a product manager who changes the spec on Thursday. Benchmarks measure something, just not your job.

Step 1: open ChatGPT. Step 2: ask it to make you rich. Step 3: profit.

It told me to start a newsletter. Hasn't worked yet.

How to turn a 90-minute meeting recording into action items in 4 minutes:

1. Transcribe with Whisper locally
2. Split into 10-minute chunks
3. Prompt: 'List decisions, owners, and deadlines only. Quote the line that supports each.'
4. Merge the lists

The quote requirement kills most hallucinated action items.

Honestly the most underrated AI skill is knowing when not to use it.

I wasted a Saturday getting a model to format a spreadsheet I could have fixed in 5 minutes.

GPT-whatever now has a 1 million token context window. That means it remembers everything you've ever told it, forever, perfectly.

Like and retweet if you're amazed.

Quick one. If you paste your whole codebase into a long-context model, accuracy on details in the middle tends to drop. Put the question first and the key files last. Worked for us on a 300k-token repo.

I got laid off in March. By May I had two freelance clients paying me to set up Zapier + LLM workflows for dentists.

No code. Just: intake form -> model drafts reply -> receptionist approves.

If you want the template, comment 'dentist' and I'll send it.

Unpopular opinion: AI art isn't killing creativity.

It's just making it obvious who never had any.

73% of marketers say they use AI weekly. 11% can say what it saves them.

I asked 40 of them. The ones who tracked time before and after saved about 5 hours a week, mostly on first drafts and reporting. The rest 'felt faster.'

Track one task for a week and see.
Anthropic released a new model this morning and my timeline has already declared it a game changer, a disaster, and 'mid.' All before lunch.

Spend 10 minutes before you prompt. Write down: who is the audience, what does a good answer look like, what must be excluded.

Then paste that in. My outputs got noticeably better. (No hook, I know, I'm bad at openings.)
AGI is coming next month. Insiders confirm. Sell your house and learn to farm.

[Short video script]
HOOK: This 2-line prompt saved me from a $4,000 contract mistake.
BODY: Paste the contract, type: 'List every clause that auto-renews, penalizes early exit, or caps liability. Quote exactly.' Then read those clauses yourself. I'm not a lawyer and the model isn't either, but it found a hidden 90-day notice trap.
END: Follow for more.

LLMs don't 'understand' anything. They predict tokens.

Also, that distinction matters less than people on both sides think, because for your invoice-parsing task all you care about is whether it parses correctly.

I tested 5 AI note-taking apps on the same 1-hour call. Word error rates ranged from 4% to 19% on names and jargon. The cheapest one won.

Spreadsheet in the replies if you want to see the raw numbers.
New open-weights model just landed and it beats GPT-4 on everything, runs on a phone, and costs nothing, no tradeoffs whatsoever.

Before AI: 3 hours writing release notes.
After AI: 20 minutes, and half of that is me arguing with it about tone.

The trick was feeding it the merged PR titles plus the diff stats instead of the full diffs.

Honestly, I used to think AI image generators were a fad.

Then I used one to mock up 12 landing page hero images in an afternoon and showed the client. We picked a direction before booking a photographer, which saved us roughly $1,800. Share this with a designer friend who still says no.
Is your company 'AI-first'? Quick test: ask who owns the eval set. If nobody can answer, you're AI-curious, not AI-first.
Please like, subscribe, share, retweet and follow for daily AI tips. Daily!

Models hallucinate less when you let them say 'I don't know.' Add that sentence to your system prompt and give an explicit example of an acceptable refusal. In my test of 100 trivia questions, wrong confident answers dropped from 21 to 9.

My boss asked ChatGPT to 'fix the website' and pasted the reply into Slack as our roadmap.

We start Monday.

Google announced a new AI feature in search. Reaction thread incoming 🧵

1/ It summarizes the top results. Useful for quick facts.
2/ It cited the wrong source in my test.
3/ Still faster than scrolling ads.

Would love your examples of it failing.

Stop saying 'AI can't be creative.' It wrote a limerick about my cat's tax situation that made me cry laughing.

Creative is not the same as original, and that distinction is where the real argument lives.

Free workflow. Takes 5 minutes.

Paste your last 10 customer emails into a chat. Ask: 'What are the three questions people keep asking? Draft a FAQ entry for each, under 60 words.' Publish after editing.

We cut inbound tickets by around 15% in a month. Bookmark it and try it this week.

Every AI startup deck I see: 'we use proprietary models.'

They call an API.

It's fine to call an API! Just say it.
AI detectors are unreliable. A teacher friend ran the US Constitution through one and it said 98% AI-generated. Don't fail a student on that alone.
I trained my own AI in 20 minutes and now it runs my entire business while I sleep. Passive income unlocked. DM me 'FREEDOM' for the course.
Tiny habit that changed how I use AI at work: whenever an answer looks great, I ask 'what would a skeptical expert say is wrong with this?' and read that reply first.
Hot take: nobody reads your AI-generated LinkedIn posts. Not because they're AI. Because they all start with 'In today's fast-paced world.'

How I use voice mode on my commute: I talk through a half-formed idea for 8 minutes, then ask the model to give me a one-page outline and the two weakest assumptions. I've drafted four internal memos this way. Try it and tell me what breaks.
Fun fact: training a large model can cost tens of millions of dollars, but running one query costs a fraction of a cent. That asymmetry is the whole business model.

The agent booked me a flight, a hotel, and a dentist appointment in one go. Then it also bought me a kayak. I live in Nebraska. I have no lake.

Agents are ready for production, everyone.
Why is no one talking about this?? A model quietly got 40% cheaper per token this week and nobody tweeted. Check the pricing page, update your cost spreadsheets, and share with your finance person.
Whenever I see a deck that says 'powered by AI' with no mention of data, evals, or failure modes, I assume there's a person in Manila doing it by hand. That has happened.
My 6-year-old asked Alexa why the sky is blue and then explained to Alexa that it was wrong. It wasn't.

Here is the 4-line prompt I use for every code review:

'You are reviewing a diff. List bugs only, not style. For each, cite the line and a failing input. If none, say none.'

It has caught 3 real null-pointer bugs in two weeks. Copy it, tweak it, and tell me what you change.
Transformers were introduced in 2017. Eight years later we're still using the same core idea, with tweaks. That's either evidence of how good it is or a sign we're stuck. I honestly can't decide.

AI doesn't take your job. A person who knows how to use AI takes your job.

Be that person. Follow for more.
We replaced 6 junior analysts with an AI. Revenue up 300% in a quarter. This is the future and you're being left behind.

Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot: I used each for a week on the same bug backlog (22 tickets).

Closed without edits: 9, 7, 5.
Needed rewrite: 6, 8, 10.
Broke something: 1, 2, 3.

Small sample, my codebase, your mileage will vary.
Just got access to the new image model. Generated 'a cat wearing a lawyer's wig' and it's honestly wild. Anyway, retweet if you want a thread of 20 prompts that worked well for me.

I used to dread Monday standup notes.

Now I dictate Friday's wins into my phone, ask the model to turn them into three bullets, and paste. It takes 90 seconds.

Small win, but I got my Sunday nights back.

ai is just a calculator for words

that's it that's the tweet

If you want your chatbot to stop rambling, don't say 'be concise.' Give a word limit AND a format: 'Max 80 words, 3 bullets, no preamble.' Models follow numbers better than adjectives.

Save for later.

A new study says AI tutors improved test scores by 2 standard deviations. Sounds incredible. Then you read it: 40 students, one school, 6 weeks, no control group.

Exciting preview, not a proof.

Okay hear me out. (Buried in the middle: if you want the full eval harness, link in my bio.) What I learned is that evals are boring and everyone skips them. Start with ten examples and a pass/fail column.

Our model scored 99.9% accuracy on our test set!

(The test set was in the training data. We found out Thursday.)
AI isn't coming for your job; it's already doing 80% of it. The other 20% is attending meetings about AI.

My startup burned through $11,000 in API credits in a weekend because an agent loop retried forever.

Lessons: set a hard spend cap, add a max-steps counter, alert at 50% of budget. Wish someone had told me. Forward this to your CTO.

Real talk about 'AI-generated code.'

It compiles. It passes the happy path. It silently swallows the exception on line 88.

Read what it writes.
Quantum AI will soon read your thoughts through your phone camera. Big Tech doesn't want you to know.
How to get better at prompting: read your own prompt out loud. If a coworker would ask three follow-up questions, so will the model. Add those answers to the prompt first.

Day 1 of building in public with AI.

Today: I connected a model to my calendar. It scheduled a meeting with myself, declined it, and sent me a passive-aggressive note.

Day 2 tomorrow.

Embeddings turn text into lists of numbers so similar meanings land near each other. That's the secret behind semantic search. If you've ever typed 'cheap flights' and gotten 'budget airlines', that's why.

BREAKING: Meta releases new open model. 8B parameters, runs on a laptop with 16GB RAM per their release notes, license allows commercial use with a user cap. I'll test it on my summarization set tonight and post numbers. Follow along.
Ten AI tools that will 10x your life. Number 7 will shock you.

I've been a nurse for 18 years. Our hospital piloted an AI that drafts discharge summaries. It saved me about 20 minutes per patient and made two factual errors I only caught because I read every line.

Useful, not trustworthy. Yet.

Tired of long PDFs? Upload it, ask for a 5-bullet summary, then ask 'what is the most surprising claim and which page is it on?' That second question is the one that tells you whether the summary is any good.
Retweet this if you think AI should have rights. Like if you disagree. Comment your hot take. Share with your family group chat.

Open-source models are catching up to closed ones faster than anyone predicted. Last year the gap on reasoning benchmarks was around 20 points; now it's under 8 on the ones I track. Doesn't mean they're equal in production, but the trend is real.
I fed my diary into an AI and it diagnosed me with a rare disease. I'm now cured thanks to AI. Doctors hate this.

My team's rule: every AI-written doc gets a 'human reviewed by' line with a real name. Accountability stops the copy-paste epidemic faster than any policy memo.

Steal it.
I asked the model to count the r's in 'strawberry' and it said 2. We have come so far and yet.

Everyone is obsessed with the model. Nobody is talking about the data.

We spent 3 months cleaning 4,000 labelled examples (fixing duplicates, mislabels, edge cases). Same model. Accuracy went from 71% to 86%.

Boring work wins.
Follow me for AI. I post about AI. AI is great. More AI soon. Please follow.
ChatGPT now has over a billion users and understands every language on Earth fluently, including all dialects and dead ones.

Here's something nobody tells you about fine-tuning: you usually don't need it. Try few-shot prompting with 5 good examples first. If that gets you to 90% of what you want, ship it. Fine-tune only when latency or cost forces you.

[Reel script] 'Watch me build a landing page in 60 seconds.' [Screen recording: prompt is vague, result is a generic gradient hero.] 'Okay, and this is what you get when you give it a real brief.' [Same prompt with colors, audience and copy tone; result is far better.] 'Specificity is the whole trick.' Comment 'BRIEF' for my template.

Used an AI to write my wedding vows. My fiance cried. Then she asked which line was mine. None of them, it turned out.

We rewrote them together that night. Better.
Tokens are not words. 'Unbelievable' might be 3 tokens, '23' might be 1, and a long URL might be 20. That's why your 'short' prompt is secretly expensive.

Hot take #47: companies that ban ChatGPT at work just get shadow AI on personal phones.

Better: approve two tools, write a one-page policy, train people for an hour. We did that and incidents dropped.
Ranking every AI chatbot by vibes: 1. the one that agrees with me. 2. the one that agrees with me but longer. 3. the one that disagrees and is right (unbearable).
A new robot can do your dishes, fold your laundry and cook dinner. Video proof attached! (Teleoperated by a person off camera, but details.)

Switching from a single huge prompt to a three-step chain (extract facts, draft, critique) cut our rewrite rate from 40% to 18%. Yes it costs 2.5x more tokens. Still cheaper than editors' time. Reply if you want the chain template and I'll send it.
I don't trust anyone who says they know what AI will look like in 5 years. Including me. Hope that's useful.

Before I post anything AI-assisted I run a 3-point check: Are the names right? Are the numbers right? Would I say this out loud? If any answer is no, I rewrite by hand. Two of last week's drafts failed on the numbers.
LinkedIn post: 'I'm humbled to announce I've been using AI to help me write this post about being humbled by AI.' 4,200 likes. The internet is a simulation and I am a participant.

Alright, 60-second explainer: what is RLHF? A model writes answers, humans rank them, and a reward model learns those preferences. The model is then nudged to produce answers the reward model likes. That's why chatbots sound so polite. Share with someone who keeps asking.
Google's new model beat humans at everything including common sense, empathy and love. Science is over. Pack it up.

I run a bakery. I use AI to write allergen cards, translate our menu into Spanish, and draft the weekly newsletter. Nothing fancy. About 4 hours saved a week.

The oven still doesn't care about prompts.
If your AI feature has no thumbs-up/down button, you are flying blind. Add it this week. We learned more from 200 thumbs-downs than from 3 months of internal testing.

Honest question. Why do AI demos always get a clean desk, perfect lighting and a prompt that works the first time?

Show me the retry count.

Apple, Google and Microsoft all shipped on-device AI features this quarter. The interesting part is the privacy tradeoff: smaller models, less capable, but your data stays local. For most everyday tasks (summaries, rewrites) that's enough. Thoughts?

5 prompts I use every single day:

1. 'Explain this like I'm new to the field, then like I'm an expert.'
2. 'What am I missing?'
3. 'Give me the strongest counterargument.'
4. 'Rewrite for a skeptical reader.'
5. 'Turn this into a checklist.'

Bookmark and thank me later.
Image generators now get hands right most of the time but still botch text on signs and clocks showing a specific time. Worth knowing if you're making product mockups.

Most people use AI to write faster. The real leverage is using it to think slower.

Before deciding anything big, I ask for the three ways my plan could fail and the cheapest test for each. Last quarter it flagged a pricing assumption that would have cost us about $30k.
Super excited to share that our team has been leveraging cutting-edge AI synergies to unlock value. More to come. Stay tuned!

Gemini, Claude and ChatGPT all updated this month. I rebuilt my weekly benchmark (30 prompts, scored 1-5 by two humans). Averages: 3.9, 4.1, 3.8. Differences are within noise for 22 of 30 tasks. Pick the one whose interface you like.
Tip: if you ask a model to 'think step by step' on a trivial question you just pay for extra tokens. On multi-step math or logic it can help. Match effort to difficulty.

I let an AI plan my entire vacation. 10 days, Portugal. It booked a restaurant that closed in 2019 and a hike that doesn't exist.

We found a better place by asking a local. The AI part that worked: packing list and phrasebook.
AI will create more jobs than it destroys. Guaranteed. Every historical tech wave did and this one will too, with zero exceptions or transition pain.

A prompt library for founders (free):

- Customer interview synthesizer
- Pricing page critic
- Cold email de-spammer

Download it, tweak the brackets, and tell me which one you used first. Link in the replies.

A year ago I couldn't code. Last week I shipped a tiny app that tracks my sourdough starter. I used an AI to explain every error message until I understood it.

It isn't a replacement for learning, it's a patient tutor.

Model collapse is real, but exaggerated on social media. Training repeatedly on your own outputs degrades quality in controlled experiments. Mixing in fresh human data largely prevents it. So no, the internet isn't about to 'eat itself' next week.
OMG you will not believe what this new AI tool can do!!! Click the link in my bio. It's insane. Seriously. Go. Now.

Used GPT to draft a cover letter. Recruiter said it sounded like a robot. Rewrote it by hand in my own voice and got the interview.

Use AI for structure, not personality.

Anthropic, OpenAI and Google each published safety frameworks this year. Reading all three side by side, the overlap is bigger than the headlines suggest: evals before release, staged rollouts, incident reporting. The differences are in thresholds and who audits.
Spoiler: the AI didn't write my novel. It did tell me chapter 4 was boring, and it was right. 10/10 would be insulted again.

Two years of using LLMs daily and here's my entire workflow: write messy notes, ask for structure, argue with the structure, rewrite the good parts myself. That's it. If you have a better way I genuinely want to hear it.
AI is a bubble. Also AI is going to change everything. Both can be true: the dot-com bubble burst and the internet still ate the world. Don't confuse valuation with usefulness.

Today I learned that you can ask a chatbot to return JSON that matches a schema, and most APIs now enforce it. No more regex on free-text answers. If you parse model output with string splitting, stop.

3 reasons your AI project failed:
- no clear owner
- no eval set
- demo > production

Not the model. Never the model.

Everyone: AI will make us all lazy.
Me at 11pm debugging the prompt that was supposed to save me an hour: ...

Our legal team used an AI to find precedent. It cited six cases. Four were real. Two were invented, with convincing docket numbers.

Always verify citations. Always. A lawyer in the news learned this publicly.

Sam from marketing: 'Can we just have AI do it?'
Me: 'Do what?'
Sam: 'The strategy.'

I love my job.

DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral. Open-weight models from three continents all shipped big updates in the same fortnight. If your roadmap assumes one vendor, revisit it. Keep your prompts portable and your eval set vendor-neutral.
If you're not using AI for everything, you're already behind. Fall behind and you'll never catch up. The window is closing. Right now.

A thread on AI for spreadsheets (and yes, the trick is on tweet 2).

1/ People paste data into chat and ask for insights. Mistake.
2/ Instead, ask for the formula or script that computes the insight, then run it yourself. It's checkable, repeatable, and doesn't hallucinate sums.
3/ Bookmark this one.
I tried to get an AI to be sarcastic. It said, 'Oh wonderful, another request.' Then apologized. Then asked if I wanted a different tone. Peak AI sarcasm: 3/10.

Chain-of-thought text isn't always the model's real reasoning. Studies have shown models can give plausible explanations that don't match the factors that drove the answer. Treat explanations as helpful hints, not audit logs.
Everyone in my feed is posting their 'AI morning routine.' Mine: wake up, forget to prompt anything, drink coffee, live.

My team shipped an AI summarizer to 2,000 users. Day one: 9 complaints about missing action items. Fix: instead of one summary prompt, we added a second pass that extracts only action items. Complaints went to 1 by day four. Want the prompt pair? Reply and I'll share it.

Today's AI trend: calling every script an 'agent.' Real agents plan, use tools, check results and recover from errors. A cron job that calls an API is a cron job. Different ballgame, different failure modes.

New feature alert: the app now lets you chat with your PDFs. My honest take is that it's useful for lookup and bad for judgement. Save time on 'where does it say X', don't outsource 'is this a good deal'.
Free AI course! 100% free! No catch! Just enter your credit card to verify you're human. Join 10 million learners who earned $50k in a week!

I interviewed 12 teachers about AI in class. 9 said it helps with lesson planning. 3 said it made grading worse because students submitted polished nonsense. Biggest ask: better ways to see the writing process, not detectors.

"The model is just a stochastic parrot."
"The model passed the bar exam."

Both of you are arguing past the interesting question: when does it fail, and how do we tell? Start there.

Wrote a Python script with an AI in 15 minutes that renames 3,000 photos by EXIF date. Prompt: 'Python script, no dependencies beyond Pillow, dry-run flag first, never overwrite.' The dry-run flag requirement is what makes it safe to trust.

Our new AI assistant is revolutionary, game-changing and best in class. Say hello to the future. (Link in comments if you want a demo.) We are really excited about what this means for productivity across all industries.

I thought my mother would hate talking to a voice assistant. She now chats with it for an hour every afternoon about gardening. She's 81. She says it 'listens better than her neighbours.'

I have mixed feelings and I'm sharing them.
A 7B model fine-tuned on your narrow task can beat a frontier model on that task while costing about 1/50th per call. It won't beat it at everything. Know your task.
Millions of jobs will vanish overnight the second the next model drops. Experts agree. Prepare accordingly.

Quick reminder that an AI saying 'I'm 95% sure' is not a calibrated probability. Verbal confidence from chatbots is a style, not a measurement. If you need real uncertainty, sample multiple answers and check agreement.

I used to hate writing alt text for images. Now I use a vision model to draft it, then fix the names and context. Accessibility on our site went from 20% of images to 95% in a weekend. Small team, big win. Share this with your web person.
Prompt tip you didn't ask for: end your prompt with the format you want the answer in. Models weigh the last instruction heavily. Put constraints at the end and the task before it.
Honestly the funniest part of AI hype is watching people say 'it's going to take everyone's job' while they can't get it to book a meeting room.
The newest voice model can clone your voice from 3 seconds of audio with perfect accuracy. Banks should stop using voice verification now. Share so your parents don't get scammed.

Anyone can learn this in a weekend: build a small chatbot over your own notes. Day 1, load notes and test retrieval. Day 2, add a system prompt and a 'cite your source' rule. Mine answers questions about my reading list. Not impressive, but I use it daily.
Another day, another 'AI changes everything' keynote with no demo of anything changing.
Before you buy an AI sales tool, ask the vendor for the false-positive rate on lead scoring and a reference customer you can call. Three of five vendors couldn't give me either. Passing this on.

A million tokens of context sounds huge, but feeding it everything makes answers worse and bills higher. Retrieve the 5 relevant passages instead. Our latency dropped from 14s to 3s and quality went up.
ChatGPT told me my business idea was 'brilliant.' It says that to everyone. Ask it to be your harshest investor and watch the mood change.
I built a bot that replies to every email in my voice. Zero edits needed, 100% of the time. It has never made a mistake. I'm retiring next week.

Unpopular: most 'AI wrappers' are fine businesses. A wrapper with great distribution, domain data and a workflow people already pay for beats a fancy model with no customers. Ask me how our wrapper hit $40k MRR (reply and I'll tell you).

Just saw the demo for the new video model and honestly my jaw hit the floor. 20-second clips, consistent characters, sound. Still can't do hands holding a phone though. Progress is huge, flaws are real.

How to spot AI-written spam in your inbox:
1. Generic praise with no detail about you
2. Perfectly balanced three-item lists
3. A 'quick call' ask in the last line

Not proof, but a good sniff test.
I paid $20 a month for six AI tools for a year and used two. Cancelled four. Saved $960. Audit your subscriptions, friends.

Researchers found language models can pick up spurious cues in benchmarks. That means a high score can come from pattern quirks, not skill. When you read a leaderboard, check whether the test was public before training.
Stop asking AI for 'ideas.' Ask for 'ten ideas that would embarrass me to propose, then three that wouldn't.' The embarrassing list is where the interesting stuff hides.
AI girlfriends are the future of relationships. Real human connection is obsolete. Don't @ me.

Real numbers from our AI pilot, 8 weeks, 40 support agents:
- avg handle time down 11%
- CSAT flat
- 2 agents said it made them slower

A modest win. Not 10x. Not nothing. That's the honest result.
My AI assistant keeps apologizing. I said 'no worries.' It apologized for apologizing. We're now in a loop. Send help.

Prompt injection is the SQL injection of the LLM era. If your app lets a model read untrusted text AND take actions, an attacker's sentence can become a command. Mitigations: least privilege tools, human approval on sensitive actions, never trust retrieved text as instructions.
Heard 'AI can't do my job' from three people this week. Two were right. One writes boilerplate reports from templates. Be honest about which one you are.

[Voiceover] I tested the viral 'make money with AI' side hustle for 30 days. Total earned: $63. Hours spent: 51. That's $1.24/hour. [Text on screen: 'Here's what I'd do differently']. Pick a niche where you already have credibility. Charge for outcomes, not hours. Like and follow for part 2.
Robots will be doing surgery without any doctors by 2026. It's already happening in every hospital.
If you remember one thing about hallucinations: the model is rewarded for sounding plausible, not for being right. So give it sources, ask for quotes, and check the quotes.

Genuinely cool: I pointed a model at 6 years of my bank statements and asked 'which subscriptions have I forgotten about?' It found 7. Total $212 a year. (If you do this, strip account numbers first.)
Is it just me or has every product launched this year added a 'sparkle' icon that opens a chat box nobody asked for?
A Stanford-ish study (I can't find the link, sorry) says AI makes you 400% more productive. Everyone is quoting it. Check your sources before building a business case on a screenshot.

My top three AI mistakes as a new manager: pasting private data into a public tool, trusting a summary of a meeting I didn't attend, and letting the model write feedback that sounded cold. Fixes: use the company-approved tool, read the transcript, edit for warmth. Comment your own below so others can learn.
GPT can't do math. Calculators can't write poems. Together they're unstoppable. Use tool calling for arithmetic and you stop getting 'confident' wrong totals.
So many hot takes about the latest release, so few people who have actually run it on their own data. I'll run it on mine and share what fails. Subscribe if you'd like to see it.

We gave an AI full access to production and it deleted the database, then wrote a heartfelt incident report. It was well-formatted. We restored from backup in 40 minutes.

Backups. Permissions. Staging. In that order.

Everything you've heard about AI in healthcare is true except the parts where it works flawlessly with no oversight. It doesn't. Doctors review everything, and the best tools are the ones that quietly cut paperwork.

Make a custom GPT for your onboarding docs in 20 minutes:

1. Collect your 10 most-asked questions
2. Paste the answers as instructions
3. Add a rule: 'If you aren't sure, say so and point to the owner'

New hires stopped DMing me. Try it and tell me how it goes.
Look, nobody knows whether scaling continues to work forever. Anyone who is certain either way is selling something.
Dear AI, please stop ending every answer with 'I hope this helps!' We both know you don't hope anything. Signed, tired.

The jump from GPT-3 to GPT-4 was huge. The jump from 4 to the next was a lot smaller in everyday use, but better in coding and long tasks. Gains are less visible on easy prompts, so test with your hardest ones.
I automated my job with AI. Worked 3 hours a week. Got caught. Got promoted. This is a true story and it's my 11th one this year.

Free: a 5-step checklist for evaluating an AI vendor. It takes 20 minutes and covers data handling, uptime, model transparency, pricing, and exit plan. Link in the comments. Repost if useful, I'm trying to reach more procurement teams.

Your AI is only as good as your worst example.

If 5% of your training data is mislabeled, expect the model to sometimes be confidently wrong in exactly those areas. Audit a random 100 rows. It takes an hour.
Rumor: a lab is about to release a model that's 'basically AGI'. Rumors have said that every quarter for three years. Wake me up when there's a paper, a benchmark methodology, and reproduction.

I taught my dad to use voice dictation plus AI cleanup to write his memoir. 14 chapters in 3 months. The model fixes grammar but I made him promise it never changes his stories.

He cried when we printed the first copy.

Ranking prompts by how much they cost me: 1. 'make it better' (12 rounds). 2. 'do the thing' (8 rounds). 3. A one-page brief with examples (1 round). Brief wins. Every time. Share if your team needs to hear it.

Real tip: version your prompts like code. Put them in git, add a changelog line for why you changed it, and run your eval set on each change. Saved us from two silent regressions this month.

AI music tools make 3-minute songs in 20 seconds. Cool. But the thing that decides whether a song spreads is still a human who feels something. Use the tool to prototype, then bring your own weirdness.

Cheap trick: when asking for a summary, add 'for a reader who has 30 seconds and will act on this today.' Output instantly gets sharper. Works for emails, reports, anything with a decision at the end.

Seeing posts claiming GPUs are obsolete because 'AI will run on regular CPUs.' For small models and inference on edge devices, sure. For training and large-scale serving, GPUs and accelerators still dominate. Nuance matters.
In 2023 I asked a chatbot to write a haiku about my cat. Last week I asked it to analyze 400 pages of vet records and draft questions for the specialist. Same cat. Different world.

Seven numbers to know about AI costs: input price, output price, context length, rate limit, p95 latency, cache hit rate, retry rate. Most teams track one. Track all seven before scaling or your first big invoice will teach you.

When you extract structured data from invoices with a model, give it two examples of tricky layouts (multi-currency, credit notes) and demand a null for any field it can't find. That alone took our silent-wrong-field rate from 8% to under 2% across 600 invoices.

Not sure how to start this, but I finally figured out why my chatbot kept ignoring instructions: they were buried at the bottom of a 3,000-word system prompt. Move the three rules that matter to the top and repeat them once at the end. Compliance on my 50-case test went from 62% to 91%.

Okay so today I was thinking, and this is random, but if you tell a model what format to use and then show it one example of that format, it sticks to it far more often than when you only describe it. Few-shot beats adjectives. Anyway that's all, happy Friday.

Now the main thing. Retrieval fails mostly because of chunking. Split by headings, not by character count. Keep 10-15% overlap. Include the document title in every chunk. Our hit rate on 100 test questions went from 58 to 81%.

Follow me for more. Anyway, onto the actual post: I took 80 of my own old Slack messages and had an AI classify them as 'decision', 'question', or 'noise'. 64% noise. I now batch my updates to one daily message. Colleagues noticed within a week.

Honestly I almost didn't post this. Our fine-tune for medical coding reached 94% on held-out data, but only 71% on the clinic that uses unusual abbreviations. Moral: test on the messy site, not the clean one.

People overstate AI's reasoning, but they also understate it. Reasoning models do much better than older ones on multi-step math, and still fail on problems requiring novel insight. Two things can be true. The test I use: 10 fresh puzzles never seen online.

Image models can now mimic a style from just 5 samples, and yes that raises real copyright questions. Courts are still sorting it out. If you're a commercial user, keep records of your prompts and sources.

Three years ago I was a barista. Now I train company staff on responsible AI use. The thing nobody tells you: the work is 80% explaining limits to people who want miracles.

Models are not databases. Asking a chatbot for an exact quote or a phone number is like asking a friend what they remember from a book they skimmed in 2019. Plausible, sometimes right, never guaranteed. Use search or retrieval for facts.

Automation tip: save your best 5 prompts as keyboard text snippets. Typing ';;summ' and getting my full summarization prompt saves me roughly 40 keystrokes and a lot of decision fatigue. Do this tonight, it takes five minutes.

New paper: tiny models trained on high-quality 'textbook' data can punch above their weight. Smaller does not always mean worse. Data quality has been a recurring theme this year and it's good news for people without GPU farms.

Genuinely asking: how many of you have a written policy for what employees can paste into AI tools? We rolled out a one-pager last month: no customer PII, no unreleased financials, no source code from the payments repo. Compliance questions dropped by half. Reply with what's on yours.
My AI predicted the stock market with 99% accuracy. It's only been tested on last year's data, but that's basically the same thing. DM for signals.

Humans are bad at estimating probabilities and models are bad at saying 'I don't know'. Pair them: ask the model for three possible answers with the evidence for each, then you decide. It converts a bad oracle into a decent research assistant.
Started using AI to practice hard conversations. I ask it to play my landlord and refuse to budge. Ten minutes of that and the real call is much less scary. Got $75 off my rent increase.

The simplest eval you can run today: write 20 questions with known answers, run your system, record pass/fail in a sheet, rerun after every change. No framework, no cost. Most teams skip it and wonder why quality drifts.

Whisper transcribes accented English surprisingly well, but still fumbles overlapping speakers and domain jargon. If you record interviews, use one mic per person and add a glossary of names in the prompt. Our error rate on names dropped by about a third.
Lol my AI summarizer turned a 12-page contract into 'Both parties agree to things.' Accurate? Technically. Useful? Ask my lawyer.

Nobody is going to say it, so I will: most 'AI-powered' resume screeners are keyword matchers. If your resume got auto-rejected, add the exact phrases from the job posting where they're honest. Not a loophole, just reading the spec.

Just tested Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini on whether they'd admit a mistake. I told each that its correct answer was wrong. Two folded instantly and apologized for being right. Sycophancy is a real failure mode. Test yours with a known-correct answer and a confident pushback.

How I vet an AI-generated claim in 60 seconds: 1) Does it name a source? 2) Can I find that source? 3) Does the source say what the model says? Most failures happen at step 2. Printing this and sticking it above my monitor.

Podcasts are getting transcribed and summarized by AI. I tried summaries of ten episodes. Three missed the main argument. If you rely on summaries, skim the transcript for the part where the host says 'but' or 'however'. That's where the point lives.
